title: Entropic Confinement and Mode Connectivity in Overparameterized Neural Networks
claim: Curvature variations in a landscape generate entropic forces that bias noisy dynamics toward flatter, broader regions, even when the energy is nearly flat.
layout: 2 panels side by side, labeled (A) and (B); left is a 3D potential surface with colored paths, right is a top-down diffusion trajectory in a tapering channel
description: Two panels. Panel A is a 3D rendered surface in a blue-to-pale-green colormap. It is a double-well or ring-shaped potential with a central ridge and a circular minimum. Two paths follow the valley floor: a yellow path in the flatter region on the left and a red path in the sharper region on the right. A dashed red arrow with arrowheads curves along the bottom from the red side toward the yellow side, which shows the bias toward flat regions. Panel B is a top-down view of a channel that tapers from wide on the right to narrow on the left. A cloud of Brownian particle positions is drawn as circles, coloured from dark purple on the left (early) to yellow on the right (late). The cloud spreads out as it moves into the wider region. The eye goes first to the 3D surface and the bright colored paths.
caption: Curvature produces an entropic force. (A) Illustration of a potential V (r, θ) with a circular minimum at r = 1, where the curvature varies with angle. At zero temperature (T = 0), the angular distribution is uniform, P(θ) = 1/(2π). At finite temperature, thermal fluctuations bias the system toward flatter regions (yellow) rather than sharper ones (red). (B) Example of a Brownian particle diffusing along the ridge of a loss landscape, lighter colors correspond to larger times. En- tropic forces generated by fluctuations push the particle toward flatter directions, effectively favoring broader regions of the landscape.
abstract: Modern neural networks exhibit a striking property: basins of attraction in the loss landscape are often connected by low-loss paths, yet optimization dynamics generally remain confined to a single convex basin and rarely explore intermediate points. We resolve this paradox by identifying entropic barriers arising from the interplay between curvature variations along these paths and noise in optimization dynamics. Empirically, we find that curvature systematically rises away from minima, producing effective forces that bias noisy dynamics back toward the endpoints - even when the loss remains nearly flat. These barriers persist longer than energetic barriers, shaping the late-time localization of solutions in parameter space. Our results highlight the role of curvature-induced entropic forces in governing both connectivity and confinement in deep learning landscapes.
